title: K-Means Clustering
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and boundaries of k-means clustering.
Apply or inspect a Scikit-learn API or workflow related to k-means clustering on a small example.
Identify a relevant assumption, validation need, or failure mode and document how to check it.

content.intro: This lesson covers K-Means Clustering in the Unsupervised Learning and Anomaly Detection module. It preserves the source syllabus topic and subtopics, then adds an original explanation, a runnable reference example, and a practice task.
content.why_it_matters: Unsupervised methods find structure without using a provided target label. Scaling and distance geometry matter; evaluate cluster quality and stability instead of assuming labels are objectively correct.

content_blocks.title: K-means loop
content_blocks.alt_text: K-means loop: Choose k initial centers; Assign rows to nearest center; Recompute centroids; Repeat until stable; Inspect clusters and limitations. Scale features when distances require it.

content_blocks.title: Practice reasoning
content_blocks.text: The example groups nearby one-dimensional points into two clusters. Cluster labels are arbitrary identifiers, not ordered classes. For k-means clustering, keep the problem definition, data selection, estimator configuration, and evaluation criterion explicit. When results are uncertain, compare a baseline and inspect examples rather than treating one metric as a complete explanation.

content_blocks.code:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
X = [[0.0], [0.2], [0.1], [8.0], [8.2], [8.1]]
model = KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=10, random_state=4).fit(X)
print(len(model.cluster_centers_))
